transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, Paint Booth 4 was stopped this morning after solvent was found pooled beneath its circulation manifold. The booth is currently isolated and the spill area is cordoned off. I'll be making the final decision on containment, restart authorization, and the recovery plan, but I need input from all of you before we can move forward. The restart authorization policy requires findings from maintenance, environmental compliance, production, and quality to be attached to the incident form before I can finalize anything. So let's start working through this systematically. Can maintenance give me an update on the equipment inspection and repair status?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed the inspection this morning. I found a cracked manifold isolation valve seat. Replacing the valve requires exactly 4 hours, and maintenance's lockout worksheet identifies exactly 6 isolation points. I have not yet attached the worksheet to the incident record. I want to be clear: because the valve seat is cracked, Booth 4 must not be authorized to restart regardless of whether the documentation entries are later completed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my environmental compliance findings. My measured cleanup estimate is exactly 240 liters of solvent-contaminated liquid. Because this exceeds the plant's hazardous-waste threshold, it requires a licensed hauler and a hazardous-waste manifest. I confirmed the threshold with the waste contractor today, but I have not yet entered the estimate in the waste log. I'll get that documented as part of the hazardous-waste handling entry on the incident authorization form.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I've got a production update. I confirmed with the scheduling desk that Booth 2 can run exactly 180 affected units per shift on both Wednesday and Thursday, which means we can reroute exactly 360 units from the Booth 4 schedule to Booth 2 without exceeding its approved rate. I haven't revised the production board yet, but this gives us a viable recovery path for the affected production.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share my quality findings. This morning I completed wipe sampling and found solvent residue on exactly 36 panels that were staged beside Booth 4. Those 36 panels must remain on quality hold and receive solvent-residue inspection before they can be released. I completed the sampling this morning but have not yet issued the hold tags. This needs to be documented as part of the disposition of potentially contaminated panels entry on the incident authorization form before Booth 4 can be restarted.
transcript.speaker: A5
